title: HubSpot implementation and onboarding | Stacktik
metaDescription: HubSpot implementation for sales and customer-facing teams: pipeline, data migration, calling and outreach connected, training. Fixed fee in writing.
h1: HubSpot implementation, built around how your team sells.
lede: HubSpot implementation is the work of turning a HubSpot account into the CRM your team runs on: pipeline stages, properties, your data moved over, calling and outreach connected, reports built and people trained.

summary.label: What it is
summary.text: Setting HubSpot up as a working CRM: pipeline stages, properties, data moved over, calling and outreach connected, reporting built and the team trained on it.

summary.label: Who it is for
summary.text: Sales and customer-facing teams that are moving to HubSpot, need the HubSpot setup done properly, or already run it and want it fixed.

summary.label: What you get
summary.text: One technical RevOps consultant from the first call to handover, a written scope, training on your own data recorded for the team, and handover notes.

summary.label: How it is priced
summary.text: Implementation is a fixed fee quoted in writing before work starts. HubSpot itself stays on the vendor's own plan and pricing.

blocks.intro: Every project is scoped on the proposal, so the list below is what we draw from, not a fixed package.

items.title: HubSpot CRM setup: pipeline and properties
items.body: Pipeline stages with written rules for when an opportunity moves forward, and the properties your team fills in on each record.

items.title: HubSpot migration: your data moved over
items.body: Data migration from your current system or spreadsheets, with duplicates merged. Salesforce and ERP migrations are not usually in scope, so ask on the call.

items.title: HubSpot integrations: calling and outreach
items.body: The phone system connected to HubSpot, so calls are logged on the record with the recording attached. Email sequences that stop when a reply comes in.

items.title: Reporting and the revenue scoreboard
items.body: Targets per rep and per team, a live leaderboard of calls, booked meetings and closed sales, and the reports the owner actually reads.

items.title: AI agents and custom tools
items.body: Agents on Claude or OpenAI write call notes, qualify inbound leads and draft follow-ups for a rep to approve. Where no platform fits, we build the tool.

items.title: Training and handover
items.body: Training sessions on your own data, recorded for the team. Handover notes say how each piece runs and who to call.

blocks.intro: A HubSpot consultant sets HubSpot up around how a team sells and supports, then connects it to the tools around it.

items.title: Maps how your team works today
items.body: We start from how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team.

items.title: Puts the scope in writing first
items.body: The proposal states what is in scope, what is not, what an addition would cost and what counts as done.

items.title: Builds it, without handing it off
items.body: The same person is on the call, the proposal and the build.

items.title: Works across every tool, not one vendor's
items.body: Setup, data, connections and training cover the whole stack: the CRM, the phone system, the outreach tool and the reporting.

blocks.h2: HubSpot onboarding: the vendor, a consultant or an agency.
blocks.intro: HubSpot onboarding services come from more than one place: the vendor, an agency, or a consultant such as Stacktik.

items.title: When HubSpot's own onboarding is enough
items.body: If HubSpot is the only tool involved and nothing else has to connect to it, HubSpot's own onboarding may be the better path. We say so.

items.title: When a consultant fits better
items.body: When the work crosses tools: data coming from another system, a phone system to connect, sequences in an outreach tool, and reports pulled from all of them.

items.title: When a HubSpot agency fits better
items.body: If you need email copy written or outbound run for you, look for an agency. That work is not usually in our scope.

items.title: Buying HubSpot: through us or direct
items.body: We handle the purchase through a vendor program where it helps, or tell you to buy direct. The proposal states our relationship with HubSpot.

items.title: When to keep the CRM you have
items.body: If connecting and fixing your current CRM solves the problem, the proposal says to keep it and lists what to connect.

blocks.h2: How Stacktik runs a HubSpot setup, step by step.
blocks.intro: The exact steps, their order and what we need from your team are written on the proposal for your project.

items.title: A free first call
items.body: We go through what you use today, what isn't working and what you are trying to get to.

items.title: A written proposal
items.body: If there is a fit, the proposal states the monthly software cost, the scope of the implementation and its fixed fee.

items.title: HubSpot set up in your account
items.body: We work inside your account through an admin seat you create for us.

items.title: Data moved, tools connected
items.body: Your data is migrated with duplicates merged while the old system stays read-only. Calling, outreach and reporting are connected to HubSpot, and each automation is documented.

items.title: Team trained, system handed over
items.body: Your team is trained on their own data and the sessions are recorded. Handover notes say how each piece runs and who to call.

items.title: Monthly support, if you want it
items.body: Optional, for teams that want the people who built the system to keep it current.

platforms.h2: The platforms we work with around HubSpot.
platforms.intro: HubSpot is the CRM, the system the others connect to.

faq.q: How much does HubSpot implementation cost?
faq.a: It depends on the scope, so there is no price on this page. Stacktik quotes HubSpot implementation as a fixed fee, in writing, before work starts, with what is in scope, what is not and what an addition would cost.

faq.q: How does a HubSpot CRM implementation work?
faq.a: At Stacktik, it runs as a call, a written proposal, then the build. On the free first call we go through what you use and what isn't working. The proposal sets the scope, the fixed fee, the steps and their order.

faq.q: How do I choose a HubSpot implementation partner?
faq.a: Choose on what the firm will put in writing. Here, implementation partner means the firm doing the setup, not a vendor partner tier. Ask what is in scope, whether the fee is fixed before work starts, whether the person on the call does the build, and whether the vendor pays the firm anything.

faq.q: Do I need a HubSpot expert, or is HubSpot's own onboarding enough?
faq.a: Not always. HubSpot's own onboarding covers HubSpot, so it may be enough when nothing else has to connect to it, and we say so. Outside help fits better when the work crosses tools: data from another system, calling, outreach and reports.

faq.q: Do we have to buy HubSpot through Stacktik to get it set up?
faq.a: No. Buying and implementation are separate, and neither requires the other. You can buy HubSpot direct and hire Stacktik only for the implementation. Where a vendor program helps, we can handle the purchase, and you can still run the setup yourself.

faq.q: Can you fix a HubSpot account we already have?
faq.a: Yes. Stacktik works with HubSpot accounts that are already set up. On the first call we go through what you use and what isn't working. If there is a fit, the written proposal says what to keep, what to connect and what, if anything, to replace.
